policy_context: STABILITY.md section 2: changing a public signature, adding #[non_exhaustive], changing what a default feature enables, or changing which requests are rejected is a minor (0.y) bump, never a patch.

STABILITY.md section 3.1: a removed or renamed item stays one minor release with #[deprecated(since, note)] first; section 3.2: at most one breaking minor per calendar month. 0.15.0 shipped 2026-10-25; a 0.16.0 in November is the month's one breaking window. After 0.16.0 ships the next one is December at the earliest (or needs a 'Cadence exception' line).

Every crate's Cargo.toml already reads 0.16.0 (crates/a2a-protocol-*/Cargo.toml:6) against 0.15.1 on crates.io (per CHANGELOG), so the cargo-semver-checks job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:985-999, all four published crates, all features) reports any break as a 'major change' and passes. Nothing below would be blocked by CI before 0.16.0 is published; every API break below is blocked after it (it would need 0.17.0). Each deliberate break still needs a '### Breaking Changes' entry and an upgrade-guide section (book-tests/tests/upgrading_guide.rs enforces a section per breaking minor; book/src/reference/upgrading/0.15-to-0.16.md lists six items today, covering G-03 and G-11 from this report and none of the rows below).

The SDK prelude (crates/a2a-protocol-sdk/src/lib.rs:100-120) re-exports EventStream, EventEmitter, agent_executor!, Server, serve, serve_with_addr, Telemetry, A2aRouter: a rename or deprecation in the server or client crate must keep the SDK re-export compiling.

new_findings.where: crates/a2a-protocol-client/src/transport/grpc.rs:304 (.timeout(config.timeout) on the tonic Endpoint) with :678-683 (req.set_timeout(send_timeout)); tonic 0.14.6 (Cargo.lock) src/transport/channel/service/connection.rs:73 and src/transport/service/grpc_timeout.rs:47-56; tonic src/status.rs:644
new_findings.finding: The gRPC channel is built with Endpoint::timeout(request_timeout) (30 s default, builder transport_factory.rs:208). tonic's client stack wraps every call in GrpcTimeout, which uses the SHORTER of the channel timeout and the request's grpc-timeout header. So the send_timeout (600 s) that grpc.rs:682 puts on a blocking SendMessage is capped at 30 s: the call fails with TimeoutExpired, which tonic turns into Status::cancelled("Timeout expired"), which this client maps to ClientError::Protocol(InternalError) saying the call was 'cancelled by the peer' (status_to_error; pinned by the test at grpc.rs:1396-1405, which also asserts !is_retryable()) - not Timeout, not retryable, blaming the agent, and without the actionable message. The outer tokio::time::timeout(send_timeout) at :643-656 never fires.
new_findings.scenario: An LLM agent over gRPC whose turn takes longer than 30 s, called with a blocking send_message (return_immediately unset) and default timeouts: fails at 30 s with a protocol error while the task keeps running on the server and the caller never learns its id - the audit D-01 failure that 57f034e fixed for JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON and WebSocket. Streaming establishment is capped the same way (a stream whose response headers take longer than request_timeout).
new_findings.probe: none needed: a gRPC case in tests/blocking_send_timeout.rs (build_grpc with with_timeout(500 ms), a 1.5 s turn) should fail today; fix by building the channel with the larger of the two (or no channel timeout, relying on per-request grpc-timeout headers already set at :452 and :682)

new_findings.finding: G-02 was fixed for Server only (serve/graceful/mod.rs refuses max_connections 0 and clamps to Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS at :326-327). GrpcDispatcher::with_max_connections and WebSocketDispatcher::with_max_connections still pass the value straight to tokio::sync::Semaphore::new: usize::MAX (or anything above MAX_PERMITS = usize::MAX >> 3) panics, and 0 builds a listener that never accepts and never says why.
new_findings.scenario: A deployment that writes with_max_connections(usize::MAX) to mean 'unbounded': the gRPC serve future panics at start (inside a spawned task for serve_with_addr / serve_with_listener, so the listener is silently gone); with 0 (e.g. from an unset environment variable parsed to 0) the WebSocket or gRPC listener accepts nothing.

new_findings.finding: With turn claims (on by default for the bundled PostgreSQL and SQLite stores), an executor that returns Ok(()) without a terminal state (G-21) releases its claim at turn end; the reaper then finds a submitted/working task with no live claim and ends it failed, class transient, with REASON 'the replica running this task stopped before it finished ... sending it again may succeed'. The same bug is silent and permanent on the in-memory store.
new_findings.scenario: Several replicas on PostgreSQL, an executor that forgets emit.status(Completed): ~15 s (claim TTL) later every such task fails with a message blaming a replica crash, operators chase non-existent restarts, and clients retry a 'transient' failure that reproduces deterministically. Behaviour differs by store for the same executor.
